newsitem.title: UK: British naval ships head to Asia-Pacific.
newsitem.headline: British naval ships head to Asia-Pacific.

text.p: Britain said on Wednesday it would send a 20-ship naval force to the Asia-Pacific area for much of 1997 to show its continued commitment to the region.
Led by the aircraft carrier Illustrious, the group will comprise surface ships, submarines and support vessels, the government said in a statement.
"Ocean Wave '97" will set off from Britain on January 13 and return in August.

"The aim of Ocean Wave '97 is to demonstrate the UK's continuing commitment to the region and the Royal Navy's ability to deploy an operationally effective and self-sustaining maritime force for a prolonged period," the government said.
" This force demonstrates the three key capabilities of the Royal Navy, namely a carrier task group, nuclear-powered submarines and amphibious forces."

The group will take part in several manouevres, including an air-defence and anti-submarine exercise with forces from Malaysia, Singapore, Australia and New Zealand, and an amphibious exercise with Brunei.

Among countries the task force is expected to visit are Abu Dhabi, Pakistan, India, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, Indonesia, Japan, Vietnam, South Korea, Russia, the Philippines, New Zealand, Australia and South Africa.
